prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE highly convincing in-game screenshot for an original premium TOP-DOWN 2D creature-collecting adventure RPG for iPad and iPhone, ages 9–12. Working title WILDBOUND. Landscape 16:10 composition. This is an actual gameplay screen filling the entire image, NOT a marketing poster, NOT a device mockup, NOT an isometric diorama. The title should be a small polished wordmark in the upper left HUD, not a large heading.
Art direction: exceptionally crafted crisp pixel art, original 32-bit handheld-era RPG feeling with modern lighting and beautiful cohesive tiles. Strict consistent top-down / overhead three-quarter 2D tile-map camera, square tiles, no perspective vanishing point, no isometric diamond grid. Readable small player sprite with blue adventurer jacket and red backpack, visible from above, and a small original companion beast beside them: a moss-backed quadruped with antler-like leaf shoots and teal eyes, no resemblance to existing franchise creatures. Other original creatures: amber shelled six-legged beetle and tiny lavender feathered lizard. Young adventurous cool mood, not preschool.
LOCATION: "Mossfall Route". A real traversable map with winding tan paths leading north from a small coastal village at lower left through deep forest to a mysterious ancient stone ruin in upper right. Distinct tiles: flowers, clustered tree canopies, tall grass patches, shallow teal river, wooden footbridge, cliff ledges and steps. One side route blocked by a thorny vine gate with a faint green creature-ability symbol. A rival trainer sprite waits across the bridge and one creature visibly peeks from tall grass. Roofs of two cozy buildings and a healing outpost at lower left. In the upper third, a distant mysterious stone door is visible within the same overhead map, no horizon sky. A fallen log forms a possible shortcut. Map must be readable with believable continuous paths and collisions. The player and moss companion stand near the vine gate at central foreground; a small contextual pill beside gate reads exactly "Use Vinecut".
AUTHENTIC TOUCH UI: top left small title "WILDBOUND" and beneath it compact location chip "Mossfall Route". Top right slim objective chip "Find the old observatory" and map icon. Bottom left translucent virtual thumbstick. Bottom center compact dark navy party strip with THREE distinct original creature portraits, small level labels "Lv. 8", "Lv. 6", "Lv. 5" and thin green HP bars. Bottom right two generous translucent touch buttons labeled "A" and "B", with A lightly glowing near the gate. Tiny bag and journal icons near top right. All interface stays inside safe margins and occupies less than 20 percent of screen; main world is uncluttered and takes priority. Restrained dark-blue HUD frames, warm gold details, readable type. Do not show coins, shop, ads, timers, battle menu, desktop windows or a large screenshot title. No existing franchise logos, characters or capture-ball imagery. Final image must look like a plausible finished top-down monster RPG that a 10–12 year old would actively want to explore, with clear adventure, discovery, team progression and visual mystery.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE high fidelity landscape 16:10 in-game screenshot for an original TOP-DOWN 2D RPG for ages 9–12 called SCRAPWILD. Full-bleed actual gameplay screenshot, NOT a poster, NOT a hardware mockup, NOT isometric. A real top-down tile-based adventure RPG with small player and NPC sprites, consistent overhead three-quarter camera and crisp beautifully crafted pixel art in a premium 32-bit handheld RPG style with restrained modern lighting.
CONCEPT: explore a frontier of overgrown machine ruins, salvage parts and build a team of quirky robot companions for turn-based battles. Robot silhouettes visibly combine swappable chassis, movement system and tool; original designs only. Color palette warm rust, mint vegetation, navy metal, amber lights, clear turquoise water. Adventurous, clever, cool, not preschool or industrial grimdark.
PLAYABLE MAP LOCATION "Rustwater Outpost": a lively frontier workshop town built around an old dried canal. Rectangular orange-roofed repair shops along upper left, open workshop to upper right displaying an unoccupied workbench and hanging chassis parts, connected walkable paths, a small bridge over a narrow canal, stairs into a lower salvage yard, stacked scrap-metal fences and tufts of vegetation. Upper center a closed steel gate marked with a lightning-bolt emblem leads toward a dark overgrown factory route. Center player sprite in teal jacket with tool backpack stands facing gate. Beside player is a small original four-legged robot with a rust-red crab-like body, amber eye strip and magnet arm. A taller rival NPC with a sleek white wheeled robot waits near the workshop. An excavated glowing blue power core is visible behind a fence as a discovery hook. No guns, violence or large illustrated foreground characters. Plausible walkable map paths and spatial hierarchy.
UI: small wordmark "SCRAPWILD" top left above location chip "Rustwater Outpost". Compact objective top right "Power the north gate" beside mini-map icon. Context action pill beside gate "Use Spark Coil". Bottom left translucent virtual thumbstick; bottom center dark navy party strip containing THREE DISTINCT robot portrait slots with tiny readable labels "Lv. 9", "Lv. 7", "Lv. 6" and green HP bars. Bottom right large translucent round "A" and "B" touch controls. Tiny wrench and backpack icons top right. Keep all UI within safe margins and under 20 percent screen coverage. Sharp readable letters, functional polished interface. No shops or currency HUD, no pay-to-win icons, no arrows plastered on the map, no battle inset or marketing copy. The screenshot should communicate a substantial explorable top-down RPG world with robot customization and a reason to walk through the gate.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE realistic finished-game screenshot for an original TOP-DOWN 2D supernatural adventure and creature-team RPG for ages 9–12 called AFTERBELL. Landscape 16:10 full-bleed gameplay screen, NOT a poster, NOT a device mockup, NOT isometric, no split-screen. Pixel-perfect detailed original 32-bit-style pixel art with a consistent top-down overhead three-quarter tile-based camera. Compact player sprite, real walkable streets and tiles, not a giant painterly character illustration.
CONCEPT: after school, ordinary neighborhoods reveal secret spirit routes; befriend strange spirits, build a team and solve a town mystery through exploration and turn-based duels. Friendly mystery and playful eerie atmosphere, no horror, no danger to children.
MAP "Lantern Street": beautiful small-town street at blue-hour dusk, warm-lit corner convenience store upper left, fenced school playground upper right, bike racks, basketball hoop, paper lanterns, tidy sidewalks, crosswalk, streetlights, autumn trees and a narrow alley between two buildings at center. Main player is a small young adventurer sprite wearing a yellow jacket and backpack, standing outside the alley with an original fox-sized companion spirit shaped like a dark blue long-tailed moth-cat with mint wing-shaped ear tufts and softly glowing amber eyes, not resembling any existing franchise character. A friendly rival kid sprite waits by the park entrance. Alley wall contains a shimmering teal doorway where a mundane brick wall has opened into a secret spirit passage; beyond the threshold tiny floating lantern spirits and luminous stepping stones are visible within the same overhead map. A second tiny umbrella-shaped spirit waits beside a puddle near the shop. Secret passage creates a strong exploration hook, but town remains the majority of screen, no horror imagery.
TOUCH GAME HUD: small stylish wordmark "AFTERBELL" upper left and location chip "Lantern Street". Upper right quest chip "Follow the lantern trail" with journal and map icons. Context pill next to doorway reads "Enter Spiritway". Bottom left translucent virtual thumbstick. Bottom center compact party strip with THREE distinctive original spirit portraits and tiny levels "Lv. 7", "Lv. 6", "Lv. 4" plus thin green HP bars. Bottom right large translucent round "A" and "B" controls, A subtly glowing. All HUD inside safe margins, restrained plum and cream frames, less than 20 percent screen coverage, crisp type. No coins, ads, chat, phone hardware, game-cover typography, school quiz elements, massive dialogue panel or copied franchise symbols. Actual screenshot should feel like an absorbing premium top-down RPG a tween could play for hours, with original characters, a cool team and mysteries around familiar corners.
